thread_relation: cross-block (the writer is a lagging warp of a non-last block A, the reader is the last block B; within block A the ordering that is missing is cross-warp: thread 0 vs the lagging warp)
thread_pair_example: driver default (grid (25,2), 512 threads, 8-bit pass): block A = any block of row r that is not the last to finish: thread 33 (warp 1) executes the L322 atomicAdd on histogram[33] while thread 0 (warp 0) of A has already passed __threadfence (L750) and executed atomicInc(&counter->finished_block_cnt) at L754 (no barrier between L750 and L754). Block B = the block whose atomicInc returns gridDim.x-1: thread 33 of B reads histogram[33] at L361 (volatile, in scan) and, after the scan, histogram[33]/histogram[32] at L383/L382 (plain, in choose_bucket); that read is not ordered after A's thread-33 atomicAdd.
class_reason: record: SC for the pair atomicAdd (L322, ATOMG.E.ADD.64.STRONG.GPU) vs the volatile load in scan (L361, LDG.E.64.STRONG.SYS) because both accesses are strong; DR for the pair atomicAdd vs the plain loads in choose_bucket (L382/L383, LDG.E.64 without .STRONG) because one access is plain (D20). Verified in the SASS of the sm_89 build.
buggy_expected: cross-block, global-memory: SC for atomicAdd (L322) vs the volatile load in scan (L361), and DR for atomicAdd (L322) vs the plain loads in choose_bucket (L382/L383). A detector that reads the SASS must find the fence (MEMBAR.SC.GPU, L750) followed by thread 0's ATOMG.E.INC.STRONG.GPU (L754) without a CTA barrier in between, i.e. nothing orders the other warps' L322 atomics before the signal.

fixed.reason: the fix inserts __syncthreads() (select_radix.cuh L760 of the fixed file, preceded by a 9-line comment L751-759) between __threadfence() (L750) and thread 0's atomicInc (L764), so every thread's L322 atomics and fence precede the signal. SASS of the fixed build: MEMBAR.SC.GPU (0x5160), ERRBAR, CCTL.IVALL, WARPSYNC 0xffffffff, BAR.SYNC.DEFER_BLOCKING 0x0 (0x51b0, line 760), then thread 0's ATOMG.E.INC.STRONG.GPU (0x5280). Reader side (not changed by the fix): the last block reads after a relaxed atomicInc (ATOMG.E.INC.STRONG.GPU) with no acquire fence, so a strict-PTX detector may still report the same pairs (L322 vs L361 SC, L322 vs L382/L383 DR) in the fixed build; that would then be a residual present in BOTH versions (idiom artifact), see open_questions.

open_questions: The oracle spec asks for exactly the two access sites of the racing pair; this target is DR+SC, i.e. two pairs that share the writer site L322 (SC with L361, DR with L382/L383). They are listed as three sites plus a 'pairs' array.

Fixed build: whether the evaluated detector models the last-block idiom (fence, barrier, relaxed ATOMG.E.INC by thread 0, __syncthreads_or, then plain/volatile reads by the last block) as ordering. The reader side has no acquire fence after the atomicInc in either version; a strict-PTX detector would then report the same pairs in the fixed build too (residual in both versions, not caused by the bug). 'absent' follows verify.expected_report_fixed (writer side fixed).

The driver uses IdxT=int64_t and dense layout; the upstream flaky test (issue 2997) is SelectKCsrTest_float_int (csr layout, int index). The racy code (L321-L323, L361, L382-L383, L750-L769) is layout-independent but the SASS widths (.64 here) would be .32 for IdxT=int.
